newsitem.title: POLAND: Floods recede in Polish border town.
newsitem.headline: Floods recede in Polish border town.

text.p: Flood waters eased on Monday in the Polish town of Slubice, from which more than 15,000 people were evacuated at the weekend to escape the surging river Odra.
Threats of flooding also receded in other regions along the river, which is known as the Oder in neighbouring Germany, officials said.

"The flood situation is stabilising. Slubice has so far resisted the river, whose level has begun to slowly decline. But the fight to save the sodden dikes continues," crisis committee spokesman Krzysztof Pomes told Reuters.
Thousands of people were evacuated from Slubice on the German border on Sunday as the Odra threatened to swamp the area.

The town, just across the river from Frankfurt an der Oder, may still face a renewed threat of total flooding when a second surge on the Odra, now some 200 km (125 miles) to the south, reaches the area in several days, Pomes said.

He said the floods, which were still affecting nearly 2,000 sq km (750 square miles) in southern and western Poland, were expected to ease further. Weather forecasts called for sunshine and only occasional showers in the next few days.
The authorities have ordered evacuation of several hundred people in the southeastern province of Przemysl, where the San river -- so far relatively calm -- was threatening two municipalities.

The three-week-old floods, the worst in centuries, have killed 55 people in Poland and left nearly 50,000 displaced. Independent analysts have estimated the damage at up to 7.5 billion zlotys ($2.3 billion).

Many people have been returning home to find debris, filth and dead livestock. The government has approved a relief package, including tax breaks and cheap credits, for the affected areas, but many flood victims complain the relief efforts have been chaotic.

Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz has ordered a meeting of the National Programme of Reconstruction and Modernisation Council for Monday to work out details of long-term relief and rebuilding operations.
